title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Daily urban water-demand forecasts can attain low average error while responding late when demand changes direction. This lag reduces their value for planning the next operating period.
The knowledge-based bi-correction model addresses the problem in two stages. Lag-penalty attention extracts prior sequence and feature information associated with timely demand changes. A stacked LSTM produces the primary forecast. A masked weighted Markov chain then corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Trend-sensitive evaluation
The study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows changes in demand more closely than a naive forecast. Reporting this metric alongside absolute-error measures separates response timing from average numerical accuracy.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Pressure under unobserved variation
CritiCoder considers macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain every disturbance in a water distribution system. Its Coder models the response associated with observed variables, while the Critic changes the loss so that the remaining pressure variation can be represented as an uncertain disturbance.
The comparison tests whether CritiCoder’s error increases less than conventional regression error at nodes more strongly affected by unobserved disturbances.

title: Research
text:
My current research asks how an AI model can move from scientific observations to experimentally feasible decisions. At Cornell, I am extending decision-focused learning toward physics-aware AI for materials discovery. Prediction alone is insufficient: the learned representation must improve the choice of material candidate, experiment, schedule, or control action under physical constraints.
Physical representations feed generative models, and constrained optimizers evaluate the resulting candidates to select the next experiment or design action. This chain exposes how each learned output changes a scientific decision.

title: Research
text:
Decision-focused learning
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize trains a probabilistic electricity-cost forecast against the stochastic water-supply schedule that follows. A differentiable convex upper bound on optimality gap, derived from Lagrangian duality, passes a decision-relevant training signal back to the predictor.
This formulation distinguishes prediction errors that change the selected schedule from errors that leave the decision unchanged. The same principle can support scientific decision problems in which a predictor parameterizes experiment selection or candidate screening.

title: Research
text:
Physics-aware generative modeling
Generative models can search large candidate spaces, but scientific candidates must satisfy structure and feasibility requirements. Physics-aware generation encodes these constraints and retains them during downstream ranking. For materials discovery, the constraint set may include symmetry, periodicity, composition, and experimental feasibility.
Candidate quality is measured by constraint satisfaction and by the physical or experimental decisions a candidate supports, alongside sample fidelity.

title: Research
text:
Scientific forecasting under uncertainty
The knowledge-based bi-correction model targets delayed reactions near demand turning points through lag-penalty attention and posterior residual correction. CritiCoder separates the response to measured inputs from pressure variation associated with unobserved disturbances.
These studies provide tools for scientific time series in which timing, uncertainty, and unmeasured effects determine the value of a prediction. The relevant evaluation quantity depends on the downstream scientific action rather than a single aggregate error score.

title: Research
text:
Generative decisions in physical environments
DRIFT stores local LiDAR geometry as graph memory. During recurrent diffusion denoising, the model retrieves waypoint-specific context and coordinates the trajectory with a target. This work connects generative modeling with local physical structure and explicit action generation.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Urban water supply consumes electricity throughout treatment, transport, and distribution. The resulting schedule depends on the expected electricity cost, while errors in that forecast can change operating cost and the selected schedule.
The study models the full water-supply process as a stochastic scheduling problem with uncertain electricity prices. Forecast quality is evaluated both by pointwise prediction error and by the objective value of the induced schedule.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize combines a probabilistic forecasting model with the downstream stochastic program. Its forecast distribution supplies uncertain cost parameters to the scheduler, and the resulting schedule defines the decision loss used to update the predictor.
Direct differentiation through this optimization problem is difficult. SPTO+ replaces the exact optimality gap with a differentiable convex upper bound derived from Lagrangian duality. The bound supplies a surrogate gradient while retaining the scheduling problem in the training objective.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Evaluation
Experiments on real-world water-supply systems compare forecast quality, operating cost, and decision regret. SPTO reports lower operating cost and regret than the tested two-stage forecasting and optimization baselines.
